# Dialogue And Restoration Instructions

- Diagnose and sync all audio sources before creative cutting.
- Preserve originals; process copies or versioned renders when destructive tools
  are required.
- Choose the cleanest microphone as the dialogue anchor and document rejects.
- Level-match clips before EQ, restoration, compression, or loudness work.
- Clean hum, rumble, clicks, crackle, plosives, mouth noise, clipping, phase,
  DC offset, and broadband noise conservatively.
- Back off any processing that creates metallic, bubbly, flanged, hollow,
  pumping, over-de-essed, or unnatural speech.
- Preserve cadence, emotional pauses, uncertainty, laughter, breath, and room
  tone when they carry meaning.
